lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: And you, Callidemides — how did you die? You know my story: I was sponging off Deinias, ate rather more than the human frame strictly required, and choked. You were there, after all, while I was dying.

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: I was, Zenophantus. Mine was a little less predictable. You know Ptoiodorus, I imagine — the old man?

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: The childless rich one? The one I knew you were usually hanging about with.

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: That’s the man. I cultivated him constantly, because he kept promising he would die and leave everything to me. But the business dragged on forever; the old man was outliving Tithonus. So I found a shortcut to the inheritance. I bought some poison and persuaded his cupbearer that, the moment Ptoiodorus asked for a drink — and he takes it fairly strong — he should drop it into a cup, have it ready, and hand it to him. If he did it, I swore I’d set him free.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: So what happened? Because you look very much as if you’re about to tell me something ridiculous.

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: Well. We came back from the baths, and the boy had two cups ready: one for Ptoiodorus, with the poison in it, and the other for me. Somehow — don’t ask me how — he got them mixed up. He gave me the poisoned one and Ptoiodorus the clean one. Then the old man drank, and I immediately found myself stretched out flat: a substitute corpse, dead in his place. Why are you laughing, Zenophantus? It is not decent to laugh at a friend.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: Because, Callidemides, what happened to you is excellent. And the old man? How did he take it?

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: At first he was shaken by the suddenness of it. Then, once he understood what had happened, I think he laughed too — given what the cupbearer had managed to do.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: Still, you shouldn’t have gone in for the shortcut. The main road would have got you there more safely — admittedly a little later.
